niche: Mind Hacks, AI Secrets, Bizarre Body Science & Hidden Power Dynamics

ideas.title: The Semantic Satiation Mind-Reading Test
ideas.angle: An interactive challenge where the viewer repeats a word rapidly to 'break' their brain's recognition, followed by a forced-choice prediction that works on 95% of people. Built-in comment trigger: 'Did I get you?'

hook.en: Say the word silk five times fast.

ideas.reason: Interactive 'forced choice' tests like the 'Red Hammer' are evergreen viral hits. This specific variation (Silk/Milk/Cow) is a high-velocity pattern because it triggers a physical cognitive glitch called semantic satiation, forcing a wrong answer that viewers love to comment on.
sources: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance

ideas.title: The Blinking Power Play
ideas.angle: A social power dynamic secret that teaches viewers how to spot a liar or assert dominance through blink-rate observation. It encourages viewers to test it immediately in their next conversation.
ideas.reason: Micro-behavior decoding videos have high VVSA because they offer 'secret knowledge' for social survival. Recent trends in 'Dark Psychology' content show massive engagement for specific, actionable body language cues.
sources: Joe Navarro, What Every Body is Saying (FBI Body Language Expert)
Psychology Today: Body Language of Blinking

ideas.title: The Pupil Expansion Attraction Test
ideas.angle: Reveals a bizarre biological reflex where pupils dilate by 45% when looking at someone you like. Commands the viewer to check their own eyes in a mirror or screen reflection, boosting retention.

hook.en: Your pupils just gave you away.

ideas.reason: Biological 'glitches' related to attraction and social interaction are highly relatable. The 'Check your eyes right now' command forces a physical interaction with the video, driving up the Average Percentage Viewed (APV).
sources: Eckhard Hess, Pupillometry: The Psychology of the Pupil
Scientific American: Why do pupils dilate?
